1.explanation: We wrap the standard DataTable in a custom render function so we can extract the `selectAll` action and the `selectedRows` state. Inside `<TableBatchActions>` (which normally only renders the selected-count text and batch-action buttons), we manually inject a `<Button>` next to the count. That button calls the `selectAll` action and displays the total number of rows (1228). With this pattern you can offer users the choice to expand from selecting just the current page to selecting every item across all pages.
1.bug_scenario: When you select a subset of rows on the current page the TableBatchActions bar appears with text such as “50 items selected.” The design calls for a second button immediately to the right of that text—“Select all (1228)”—so that users can escalate from selecting only the visible page to selecting every row across all pages. Clicking that button should invoke the DataTable’s `selectAll` action to select every row in the data table.
